title: The gifts come up
hookLine: bread and wine are carried forward; a drop of water mingles with the wine

lines: A FAMILY WALKS UP THE AISLE.
cards: The prayers for the world end, and the whole feel of the Mass shifts. People sit. Baskets move down the rows: the rustle of envelopes, a kid proudly dropping in a coin.
Up front, servers lay a white cloth on the altar and set down a cup and a book.
Then, from the back of the church, a few ordinary people walk up the aisle, a couple maybe, or a family with a nervous child, carrying a plate of bread and a small glass jug of wine.
They hand them to the priest and sit back down. It looks like nothing.

teach.b: Offertory comes from the Latin offerre, to bring forward, to offer. The Mass has two great halves. The first is the word: readings, homily, creed, prayers.
The second, starting now, is the Eucharist, the meal.
And it starts with ordinary people carrying up ordinary things. Bread, which the earth gave and human hands made. Wine, the same.
In the early Church, people often brought bread and wine from their own homes, and the leftovers went to the poor.
The collection is the same idea: the people's gifts, for the Church and the poor, carried up with the bread.

teach.h: A BLESSING OLDER THAN THE MASS.
teach.b: Then the priest lifts the bread a little and blesses God for it, in a prayer shaped like something much older.
It echoes the Jewish blessings said over bread and wine at the table, the ones that begin baruch atah, blessed are you, the kind Jesus himself would have said.

teach.h: ONE DROP OF WATER IN THE WINE.
teach.b: The priest or deacon pours the wine into the chalice, then adds a single drop of water.
He says a short prayer under his breath, borrowed from an ancient Christmas prayer: it asks that, since Christ came to share our humanity, we might come to share his divinity.

The water disappears into the wine, and it can't be taken back out. Catholics see in it the human joined to the divine, and some see the water and blood from Christ's side on the cross. Then the priest washes his hands.
From mercy and glory through the creed, this week the word was given.
Now the ordinary things go up.

how: At the preparation of the gifts, a collection is taken, members of the congregation often carry the bread and wine to the altar, the priest blesses God over each, adds a drop of water to the wine, and washes his hands.

practice: Think of one ordinary piece of your day: the commute, a sink of dishes, the kids' bedtime. Picture carrying it forward in your hands, like that family in the aisle, and setting it down.
If you pray, offer it to God, like a drop in the wine; if you don't, simply let it count, as part of something larger.

wordCard.voice: Offertory. The bringing forward of bread and wine, and the people's gifts, at the start of the Eucharist. Today's word.
